cold noun

the illness

also common cold, catarrh, runny nose, blocked nose, catch a cold, have a cold

classical

Catull. 44.13–14
Traupman 56: gravēdine labōrās, you’re suffering from a cold
Traupman 63: gravēdinem contrahere, to catch a cold; gravēdine labōrāre, to have a cold
Traupman 61
Traupman 293

gravēdō, gravēdinis f.

noun, third declension

heaviness, especially a cold in the head or catarrh

Useful for “a cold,” without claiming an exact ancient diagnosis of a modern viral infection. Formed from gravis, “heavy”.

Other words

  • corȳza, corȳzae f. — catarrh

    noun, first declension · also used · late Latin

    A Greek medical loan, attested in Late Latin; it represents Greek κόρυζα.

  • dēstīllātiō, dēstīllātiōnis f. — dripping or discharge; catarrh in medical contexts

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Traupman 65: dēstīllātiōnēs, runny nose

  • Gravēdine labōrō.

  • mē gravēdō frīgida et frequēns tussis quassāvit

    a cold in the head and a constant cough shook meCatull. 44.13–14

  • Nāsus fluit.

  • Nāsus obstrūctus est.

    The nose is blocked.composed
